output.summary: The ED length-of-stay rise is about 3.0 of 3.2 hours boarding, not ED work-up. ED RN hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance are flat, and volume, acuity and bed capacity are unchanged, so nurse understaffing is contradicted. Boarding jumped in March when the hospitalist rounding change began. Medical-ward discharges slipped later, while surgical wards held steady. A rotation-determined pilot on 4 West cut boarding from 4.6 to 2.3 hours. Extend the huddle to the other medical wards and track the results. Do not approve the travel nurses funded by deferring case managers, and do not pause the huddle. The cleaning-staff effect and the triage-provider effect on front-end metrics remain unknown. Evening cleaning staffing is not yet a justified primary fix.
